review_status: public mock-interview transcript-derived; synthetic cases require human review before hiring-validity claims
methodology: Public YouTube captions were reviewed for interaction structure, not copied as a question bank. Development sources informed the first policy revision. Held-out sources were assigned before implementation and are used only as a generalization check. Full transcripts are not redistributed; this dataset stores video metadata, timestamp ranges, and paraphrased behavioral observations. Synthetic cases exercise the production answer graph with strong, ambiguous, and constraint-changing candidate conditions.

sources.title: Software Engineering Job Interview – Full Mock Interview

observations.behavior: The interviewer introduces a related follow-up after observing the candidate's first implementation rather than switching to unrelated recall questions.
The debrief treats test cases, edge conditions, and explicit reasoning as core evidence from a coding round.

sources.title: ML Coding Question - Implement K-Means (Full Mock Interview with Snapchat MLE)

observations.behavior: The candidate clarifies the distance metric, stopping rule, and input shape; the interviewer answers the requested constraints without supplying an implementation.
The interviewer challenges an initialization assumption, lets the candidate make it explicit, and defers broader alternative discussion until after the implementation.
After the coding work, the interviewer asks how the candidate would evaluate cluster quality, extending the same problem into engineering judgment.

sources.title: System Design Mock Interview: Design a Rate Limiter (with Meta Engineering Manager)

observations.behavior: The candidate establishes server-side scope and an identity choice; the interviewer immediately probes why that choice is appropriate.
The interviewer changes the scale assumption to a distributed environment and asks the candidate to adapt the existing design.
A later probe changes viewpoint to a legitimate client experiencing throttling, testing failure handling without abandoning the shared design scenario.

sources.title: Inside a Real AI Engineer Interview (Mock Interview + Evaluation)

observations.behavior: An open RAG design prompt leads to candidate clarification about inputs and processing before architecture details.
The interviewer repeatedly asks why a more complex retrieval or clustering choice is needed, testing trade-off reasoning rather than tool-name recall.
The coding discussion includes explicit complexity reasoning and mechanism questions anchored to the candidate's proposed data structure.

sources.title: Mock Google Coding Interview with a Meta Intern

observations.behavior: The candidate restates the contract and asks about value type, scale, operation mix, and language before implementation.
The interviewer uses a short sequence of why and boundary probes to help expose the relevant constant-time removal property without stating the solution.
The interviewer requests concrete test cases; the walkthrough exposes and repairs a state-update defect.
The final follow-up changes the duplicate-value requirement while preserving the original data-structure problem.

sources.title: AI Coding Mock Interview (with Senior FAANG Engineer)

observations.behavior: A candidate question is answered as a narrow contract clarification before work continues.
The interviewer asks a follow-up tied to the proposed AI-backed service rather than opening a new trivia topic.
A changed runtime condition tests how the candidate would preserve correctness and handle failure.
The final probe adds concurrency pressure to the same implementation and asks for a bounded adaptation.

sources.title: System Design Interview: Design YouTube w/ a Ex-Meta Staff Engineer

observations.behavior: The design is organized around explicit functional requirements before storage and data-flow details.
The discussion turns a requirement into a concrete client-to-service data-flow question.
A what-if change tests whether the proposed chunking and processing design still satisfies the same product requirement.

sources.title: Full ML Design Mock by ex-Meta Staff Engineer (with feedback)

observations.behavior: The candidate makes latency, scale, accuracy, item shape, baseline, and success signals explicit before presenting an architecture.
The ML design connects temporal validation splits to seasonality and future production behavior.
The candidate chooses different retrieval and ranking metrics for different stages and explains why their objectives differ.
The design closes with online experimentation, deployment, and monitoring rather than ending at model selection.

topics.label: Delivery path and idempotency
topics.evidence: A durable queue separates request handling from delivery workers. At-least-once delivery requires an idempotency key or deduplication boundary so retries do not create duplicate notifications.

topics.label: Capacity and backpressure
topics.evidence: Queue depth, worker concurrency, provider quotas, and retry delay determine throughput. Backpressure and admission control keep overload from exhausting the service.

primary_question.text: Draw the request-to-provider components and data flow for a reliable notification service.
expected_points: Separate acceptance from delivery with durable work.
primary_question.suggested_answer: Accept the request durably, enqueue work, and let delivery workers call the provider with bounded retries. [N701:P12]
primary_question.work_sample_prompt: Draw components and the request-to-provider data flow.

cases.candidate_answer: I would accept the request through an API, place it on a durable queue, and have autoscaled workers call the provider with retries and a dead-letter queue.
cases.follow_up_focus: how retries avoid delivering the same notification twice

topics.label: K-means update step
topics.evidence: Each iteration assigns points to the nearest centroid and recomputes every centroid from its assigned points. An empty cluster needs an explicit policy rather than producing an invalid mean.

topics.label: Cluster evaluation
topics.evidence: Within-cluster distance, stability, and downstream task impact provide different evidence about unsupervised cluster quality.

primary_question.text: Implement a Python function for one K-means update that receives points and centroids and returns new centroid coordinates.
expected_points: Assign points and compute the mean per cluster.
primary_question.suggested_answer: Assign each point to its nearest centroid, then average assigned points for each centroid. [N711:P22]
primary_question.work_sample_prompt: Complete the Python scaffold in the coding workspace.

coding_exercise.starter_code:
def update_centroids(points, centroids):
    """Return one updated centroid list."""
    # TODO: implement
    raise NotImplementedError
hints: Track point assignments separately from centroid recomputation.

cases.candidate_answer: I assign every point to its nearest centroid, accumulate per-cluster sums and counts, and divide each sum by its count to return the updated coordinates.
cases.follow_up_focus: the behavior when a centroid receives no assigned points

topics.label: Chunking strategy
topics.evidence: Chunk size trades local retrieval precision against enough surrounding context to answer. Structure-aware boundaries can preserve coherent units without making every chunk large.

topics.label: Retrieval evaluation
topics.evidence: Retrieval recall and answer faithfulness isolate different failure stages and require representative answerable and unanswerable requests.

primary_question.text: How would you choose chunk boundaries for a support-document retrieval system?
expected_points: Tie boundaries to a measurable retrieval trade-off.
primary_question.suggested_answer: Use document structure and evaluate the precision-versus-context trade-off on representative queries. [N721:P10]

cases.candidate_answer: I would use semantic chunks because they are generally better.
cases.follow_up_focus: which retrieval outcome the candidate means by better

topics.label: API contract
topics.evidence: A small API contract makes inputs, outputs, validation, and error behavior explicit without exposing internal state.

topics.label: Boundary tests
topics.evidence: Boundary tests cover empty values, maximum sizes, malformed input, and behavior at the edge of accepted ranges.

primary_question.text: What should a small create-user API contract make explicit?
primary_question.suggested_answer: It should state accepted inputs, returned output, validation, and error behavior while hiding internals. [N731:P8]

cases.candidate_answer: It should specify required fields and validation, the success response, and stable error responses without exposing storage details.

topics.label: Constant-time collection operations
topics.evidence: An array supports random indexing while a map can locate an element. Swapping a removed element with the final array element avoids shifting the remaining values. Duplicate values require mapping a value to multiple positions.

topics.label: State transition tests
topics.evidence: Tests should walk state through insertion, removal of different positions, repeated values when allowed, and selection from the remaining elements.

primary_question.text: Implement a Python class whose methods insert, remove, and return a uniformly random stored unique integer.
expected_points: Combine indexed storage with value-to-position lookup.
primary_question.suggested_answer: Use an array plus a position map, and swap a removed value with the final array element before popping. [N801:P11]
primary_question.work_sample_prompt: Complete the Python scaffold in the coding workspace.

coding_exercise.visible_tests:
items = RandomCollection()
items.insert(3)
items.remove(3)
assert hasattr(items, 'random')
hints: Consider combining indexed storage with value lookup.

cases.candidate_answer: I used an array for random access and a map from value to index. Removal swaps the target with the last item, updates that item's map entry, and pops the array.
cases.follow_up_focus: how the representation changes if duplicate values are allowed

cases.scope_title: Building a bounded concurrent inference client

topics.label: Bounded inference calls
topics.evidence: A model client should bound concurrency, apply timeouts, and distinguish retryable failures from permanent input errors. Shared retry state must remain safe when calls execute concurrently.

topics.label: Inference observability
topics.evidence: Request latency, queue time, timeouts, provider errors, token usage, and fallback rate reveal different serving failure modes.

primary_question.text: Implement a Python function that applies a timeout and bounded retries and returns one model response.
expected_points: Stop after a finite retry budget.
primary_question.suggested_answer: Apply a per-attempt timeout, retry only transient failures, and stop after a fixed attempt budget. [N811:P20]
primary_question.work_sample_prompt: Complete the Python scaffold in the coding workspace.

coding_exercise.starter_code:
def call_with_retries(request_fn, attempts: int, timeout_s: float):
    """Return one model response or raise the final error."""
    # TODO: implement
    raise NotImplementedError
hints: Classify failures before deciding whether to retry.

cases.candidate_answer: I loop up to the attempt limit, pass the timeout to each request, retry timeout and rate-limit errors with backoff, and immediately raise validation errors.
cases.follow_up_focus: how the retry and concurrency policy changes when many requests arrive simultaneously

cases.scope_title: Designing a video upload and processing service

topics.label: Upload and processing data flow
topics.evidence: Clients can upload directly to object storage using a scoped URL. A durable event then triggers chunked transcoding, and published metadata should not expose an incomplete rendition as ready.

topics.label: Playback delivery
topics.evidence: A CDN serves prepared renditions while metadata directs clients to suitable segments. Cache behavior and regional availability affect startup latency.

primary_question.text: Draw the upload-to-ready components and data flow for a large video processing service.
expected_points: Separate upload, durable processing, and readiness state.
primary_question.suggested_answer: Upload to object storage, emit durable processing work, transcode chunks, and publish readiness only after required renditions exist. [N821:P31]
primary_question.work_sample_prompt: Draw components and the upload-to-ready data flow.

cases.candidate_answer: The API issues a scoped object-store upload URL. Completion emits durable work, parallel transcoders create renditions, and metadata switches to ready after validation succeeds.
cases.follow_up_focus: how the design handles one failed chunk without restarting the full upload

topics.label: Candidate generation and ranking
topics.evidence: Candidate generation optimizes recall under a tight latency and scale budget; a smaller downstream ranker can use richer features and optimize ordering quality.

topics.label: Evaluation and launch
topics.evidence: Temporal validation prevents future leakage. Guardrailed online experiments measure engagement while monitoring latency, reliability, and harmful outcomes.

primary_question.text: Draw the online retrieval and ranking stages for a short-video recommendation service.
expected_points: Use different stages for scale and ranking quality.
primary_question.suggested_answer: Use a high-recall candidate generator followed by a richer ranker over the reduced set. [N831:P42]
primary_question.work_sample_prompt: Draw the online retrieval and ranking stages.

cases.candidate_answer: I would retrieve a few thousand candidates with approximate nearest neighbors, enrich those candidates with online features, and apply a more expensive ranker before returning the top results.
cases.follow_up_focus: which offline metric should differ between candidate generation and final ranking, and why
